lines: Persistent cough and unexplained weight loss over 3 months

The patient is a 46-year-old male with a history of nicotine dependence, primary hyperparathyroidism, and malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes who presents to the Pulmonology clinic for evaluation of new symptoms.
He reports a persistent cough and unexplained weight loss over the past 3 months.
He denies fever, night sweats, or hemoptysis.
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (GOLD Stage II)
- Ureteroscopic stone removal (right kidney), 2 months prior
- Ibuprofen 600 mg PO PRN back pain
His family history is significant for lung cancer in his father.

A chest X-ray shows a mass in the right upper lobe, and a subsequent CT scan confirms the presence of a 4 cm mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
A biopsy of the mass is performed, and the pathology report indicates non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
The patient is enrolled in a case-control study to investigate the association between a specific genetic mutation and the development of NSCLC.
The study includes 100 cases with NSCLC and 100 controls without NSCLC.
The presence of the genetic mutation is 60% in cases and 20% in controls.
